title: Optimizing the Inert Gas Transfer of Lithium Ion Battery Materials for Examination in the Electron Microprobe/FESEM
content: The characterization of lithium and other air and water sensitive materials in engineering applications necessitates specialized atmospheric controls to prevent unwanted chemical reactions. A good case in point is the chemical analysis of lithium ion batteries in the electron microprobe. While nitrogen is commonly used for purging electron microscope vacuum systems, its reactivity with lithium to form lithium nitride presents significant challenges. This study details the optimization of the GVX plasma cleaner vacuum to pressure-trigger for argon as compared to nitrogen.
